question.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,3,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨4,0,1⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-1,3,2⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨4,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =⟨-1,3,2⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,0,1⟩ & =-2 \\ 4x+z & =-2 \\ 4x+z+2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
